source_text:
4 Ἔπρεπε γὰρ τῷ πάντα εὐπόρῳ καὶ ἐκ θελήματος ὡς ἐκ πηγῆς ἀενάου ἀναβλύζοντι τὰ ἀγαθὰ, ὑπὸ στέγην πτωχῶν εἰσεληλυθότι, προσθεῖναι τοῖς πενιχροῖς τὰ πλούσια, καθάπερ καὶ τοῖς ἐν Κανὰ Γαλιλαίας τὴν ἀγεώργητον οἰνοχοΐαν, καὶ τὸν ἀπόλυτον ἐκεῖνον εὐκαίρως εἰς μέσον ἀγαγεῖν καὶ ὡς παράδεισον πανδαισίας εὐωχοῦντά τε καὶ εὐωχούμενον διανοῖξαι τοῖς παισίν· ἐν ᾧ οὐκ ὀσμὴ φθορᾶς ἐφαίνετο· μετέλαβεν γὰρ διὰ τῆς θείας κλήσεως τῆς ἀφθάρτου εὐωδίας· οὐδ' αὖ λώβη μελῶν ἐδείκνυτο· δημιουργὸς γὰρ ἦν ὁ παροστάξει ἀναπλάσας ἀλλ' οὐδὲ μικρόν τι ἢ μέγα ὅπερ ἀλλοίωσιν τοῖς καταβιβαζομένοις διαχαρακτηρίζει, ἀλλ' ἦν
ἀκέραιον τὸ ἄγαλμα πάντοθεν ἄρτιον καὶ εὐειδὲς ἄχρι τριχός. 5 Πρεπόντως τοιγαροῦν ἐκτρέφει ἐκείνην εὐφρασίαν, φημὶ δὲ ἔκ τε τῆς τῶν ὑποδεξαμένων παναρέτων ἀκραιφνοῦς ἀγαπῆς, ἔκ τε θαυμάτων τοῦ ἀνενδεῶς ὑποδειχθέντος θεοῦ. Ἤδει γὰρ ᾔδει σαφῶς ὅτι τοῦτο μάλιστα ἐφηδύνειν εἴωθεν τὸν θεῖον ὀφθαλμὸν εἰ τὸν εὐεργετούμενον σωτῆρα .., καθῶς ἀκηκόει παρ' αὐτοῦ ὅτι «ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με,» θέλημα δὲ Πατρὸς καὶ Υἱοῦ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἡ σωτηρία. Σωτηρία μὲν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὑπάρχει ἡ εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν ἀεὶ συνδοξαζόμενον τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι ἐν ὑψίστοις πίστις, ὠς ἐν εὐαγγελίοις φησί· «τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ θεωρῶν τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.»
thought_title: Lazarus shown whole and the saving will
orientation: The preacher is still using Lazarus at table as proof that his resurrection was real, just before turning to the saying about fire.
pass_a_gloss: For it was fitting for the one rich in all things and bubbling up good things by will as from a spring that never fails, after he entered under a roof of poor people, to add rich things to the needy, just as also for those in Cana of Galilee the unplowed serving of wine, and in good season to bring into the midst that freed man and to open him to the children as a paradise of feasting of every kind, both feasting and being feasted; in whom no smell of decay was appearing; for through the divine call he had shared in the fragrance that is without decay; nor again was injury of limbs displayed; for creator was the one who at close hand formed him again; but neither small nor great thing which marks alteration in those being brought down to the grave, but the statue was unharmed, complete from all sides and shapely even to a hair. Fittingly therefore he nourishes that cheer, I mean both from the pure love of the wholly virtuous ones who received him, and from the wonders of the God shown without lack. For he knew, he knew clearly that this especially is accustomed to sweeten the divine eye, if [lacuna] the savior who is being done good to [lacuna], just as he had heard from him that my food is that I do the will of the one who sent me, and will of Father and Son is the salvation of men. Salvation of men is faith in him who always is glorified together with the Father and the Holy Spirit in the highest, as he says in the Gospels: this is the will of my Father, that everyone who looks upon the Son and believes in him may have eternal life.

choices.why: keeps the agricultural adjective literal for the Cana miracle rather than explaining it as miraculous
Lazarus was freed from death and decay, not merely dismissed
keeps ἄγαλμα in its literal sense instead of smoothing to body
preserves the metaphor of sweetening rather than reducing to pleasing

bible_refs.note: ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με
τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Πατρός μου, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ θεωρῶν τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον

pass_b_english: It was only right for him to act in this way. He holds riches for every need, and good gifts pour from his will like water from a spring that never runs dry. He had entered under a poor roof, so it was fitting for him to add wealth to their poverty. He had done the same at Cana in Galilee, when he gave wine that no field had grown. In the same way it was fitting for him to lead that freed man into their midst at just the right hour, and to lay him open before the children like a paradise of rich feasting, where he both gave joy and shared it.

In Lazarus no stench of decay remained. A divine call had given him a share in imperishable fragrance. No wound or ruin showed in his limbs. His Maker had formed him anew in a moment. No mark, small or great, was left of the kind that change stamps on bodies lowered to the grave. His frame stood whole on every side, complete and beautiful to the very hair.

So he fittingly fed that gladness. I mean it sprang both from the pure love of those blameless hosts and from the miracles of a God fully revealed. For Martha knew, she knew well, what delights the gaze of God above all else: if the Savior who has received kindness … [the text breaks off here]. She had heard this from his own lips. For Jesus says, "My food is to do the will of him who sent me" (John 4:34). And the will of the Father and the Son is the salvation of men. That salvation is faith in him who is glorified forever on high with the Father and the Holy Spirit. As Jesus says in the Gospels, "This is the will of my Father, that everyone who looks on the Son and believes in him should have eternal life" (John 6:40).
notes: After σωτῆρα the source has .. marking a lacuna; the if clause is incomplete, so the gloss leaves accusative τὸν εὐεργετούμενον σωτῆρα as object of an unfinished clause and supplies no verb.
Sense of παροστάξει is uncertain; glossed only as at close hand.

problems.quote: when one sets before him the Savior and the one who has received his kindness
problems.why: The Greek text breaks off here. The English fills the gap with a made-up claim and splits 'Savior' and 'the one benefited' into two objects without marking that anything is missing.
problems.fix: what delights the gaze of God above all else: if the one who has received kindness [shows honor to] the Savior… (the text is broken here)
problems.ruling: Source ends at εὐεργετούμενον σωτῆρα ..; English supplies 'sets before him' and a full clause without marking the lacuna.

edits.old: what delights the gaze of God above all else: when one sets before him the Savior and the one who has received his kindness.
edits.new: what delights the gaze of God above all else: if the Savior who has received kindness … [the text breaks off here].

fixed: Fixed invented completion: Greek has only εἰ τὸν εὐεργετούμενον σωτῆρα .. with lacuna, one phrase not two objects, so merged and marked break.

last_rejected.quote: if the Savior who has received kindness
last_rejected.why: εὐεργετοῦντα is active: the Savior who benefits others, not one who receives kindness.
last_rejected.fix: if the Savior who shows kindness to others
last_rejected.ruling: The source actually reads passive "τὸν εὐεργετούμενον σωτῆρα", not εὐεργετοῦντα. So "who has received kindness" is accurate; the checker misquoted the source.

last_rejected.quote: where he both gave joy and shared it
last_rejected.why: εὐωχέω means feasting and being feasted, not giving or sharing joy.
last_rejected.fix: where he both feasted and was feasted
last_rejected.ruling: εὐωχέω can mean gladden or entertain, and the passive can mean enjoy oneself. "Gave joy and shared it" stays in that range, and the nearby "paradise of rich feasting" keeps the feasting sense.
